data.name: Heading
data.value: Step 5 of 5: Signed in – the portal has its tokens

data.name: Lead
data.value: After the checked BundID response, the sign-in service signed you in and informed the portal. The portal turned this into its own session.

data.name: Flow_Callback
data.value: The sign-in service sent your browser with a one-time code and the state as a form to the portal's /signin-oidc (response_mode=form_post); the portal checked the state against its correlation cookie.

data.name: Flow_Token
data.value: The portal redeemed the code directly at the sign-in service (POST /connect/token, server to server) with its client secret and the code_verifier (PKCE). The tokens below came back.

data.name: Flow_Validate
data.value: It validated the ID token: signature with the sign-in service's key (JWKS), issuer, audience (= client ID), expiry and nonce; then it fetched further data from the UserInfo endpoint.

data.name: Flow_Session
data.value: It created its session (cookie __Host-bp-sitzung; the tokens stay on the server). From now on it calls the API with the access token.

data.name: Token_Title
data.value: What arrived in the code exchange (without the tokens themselves)

data.name: Claims_Title
data.value: What the portal now knows about you

data.name: Claims_Intro
data.value: The BundID SAML assertion (step 4) became claims in the ID token and at the UserInfo endpoint. Identifiers are shortened.

data.name: Recap_Title
data.value: The whole way in one sentence

data.name: Recap_Text
data.value: Portal → (OIDC) → sign-in service → (SAML AuthnRequest) → BundID identifies you → (signed SAML response) → sign-in service checks it and recognises you by the bPK2 → (code, then tokens) → portal. Your browser carries all messages except the token exchange; trust rests only on signatures and registered addresses.
